memory_candidates.content: A jq batched-update filter of the shape `map(if ($updates | has(.field|tostring)) then ... end)` silently no-ops: a jq function argument (has()'s argument here) is evaluated against the SAME input as the function call itself ($updates), not the outer map(.) item. Fix by binding `. as $item |` first and referencing `$item.field` explicitly inside the function argument. Caught only by an actual positive-case assertion (array populated), not by an exit-code check alone.

Before trusting a dispatch's enumerated 'consumer sites' or 'call sites' list for a live wiring task, grep for actual invocation (not just textual mentions) and check each named file's own header/doc comments for an orphaned-script or superseded-by note. In this codebase, orchestrator-postflight.sh is a fully orphaned script (zero live callers, confirmed by skill-git-workflow/SKILL.md's own 'Relationship to orchestrator-postflight.sh' section) while the actually-live equivalent (skill_postflight_update in skill-base.sh) went unnamed in a dispatch that predated a refactor. A phase's own Scope Hypothesis escape valve ('if a fifth site exists, wire it too') is the mechanism that catches this class of drift -- always exercise it literally, not just as a formality.

A test suite for a script whose sibling dependency enforces deploy-root-guard.sh (blocking source-store invocation) must drive the DEPLOYED copy of the script under test, not the source-store copy -- even when the script under test itself has no such guard, if it calls a sibling script via a same-directory relative path (e.g. $SCRIPT_DIR/state-write.sh), that sibling's guard transitively applies. The fixture then needs no script-copying at all: point --state-file (or an equivalent flag) at a throwaway fixture directory and let the deployed dependency chain resolve everything else.
